basis: Callosal agenesis in 3/3 and heterotopia in 2/3 document CNS malformations. Cancer predisposition alone is excluded; polyposis frequency is unspecified.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: definition describes cancer predisposition; polyposis is unquantified and not established as common direct gastrointestinal involvement.
decisions.neurologic: primary: structural CNS abnormalities are documented in 3/3 (callosal agenesis) and 2/3 (heterotopia), supporting a directly affected organ.

basis: Prenatal methylmercury causes developmental brain injury; hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%. Visual impairment is commonly cerebral, without established intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment (80-99%) commonly reflects cerebral injury; direct eye or optic-nerve damage is not established.

basis: Usually a deep extremity soft-tissue sarcoma; supplied HPO reports subcutaneous nodules in 80-99%, supporting tumor occupation of subcutis despite usual deep origin.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous tumor nodules are annotated in 80-99%; this supports direct subcutis occupation even though the usual primary origin is deep soft tissue.

basis: Vertebrobasilar arterial insufficiency defines posterior-circulation cerebral ischemia; both the diseased arteries and ischemic brain are primary sites.

decisions.neurologic: primary: cerebral ischemia is a defining disease process and an explicit MONDO feature; completed infarction is not required for the primary tier.

basis: Rib and palatal defects define disease; tracheomalacia and intellectual disability each occur in 30-79%. Ear atresia/hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted under cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%; its potentially substantial lifelong impairment gives it priority under the four-axis cap.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: ear-canal atresia and conductive hearing impairment occur in 30-79%; severe airway and neurodevelopmental impairment take priority.

basis: Streptococcal infection with defining hypotensive shock; renal failure occurs in roughly 70% and ARDS in roughly 50%. Coagulopathy and hepatic injury omitted under cap.

decisions.haematologic: none under cap: coagulopathy occurs in roughly half; renal failure and ARDS take priority because of severe organ dysfunction.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: ARDS directly injures lungs in roughly 50%, meeting the frequency threshold and taking priority under the cap.

basis: Immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation causes ocular motor cranial neuropathies; ophthalmoplegia reflects nerve dysfunction without established intrinsic eye injury.

decisions.ocular: none: defining ophthalmoplegia results from ocular motor cranial neuropathy; eye-movement symptoms do not establish direct damage to eye structures.

basis: Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal erythrocytes, causing severe anemia and hydrops. Edema and anemia-related circulatory stress do not establish direct cardiac injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: anemia-related high-output stress and hydrops do not establish direct cardiac injury; fluid accumulation alone is insufficient.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment characterizes the deletion spectrum; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 30-50% of reported cases, varying with deletion extent.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart malformations affect roughly 30-50% across reported 8p deletions; variable intervals warrant medium confidence.

basis: Defining eye and esophageal defects; tracheoesophageal fistula occurs in 80-99%. Callosal agenesis occurs in 30-79%; hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted under cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: tracheoesophageal fistula is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 80-99%, directly affecting the trachea.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%; defining eye, esophageal and tracheal defects plus substantial CNS abnormalities take priority.
